cues.text: This mother is blood group B, RhD-negative.
She has just given birth to a baby who is B, RhD-positive.
Through childbirth, she has been exposed to the RhD antigen.
Untreated, she would develop antibodies that would attack a later RhD-positive baby in the womb.
Anti-D immunoglobulin reduces her immune response, and so the risk of developing these antibodies.
Her haemoglobin of 11.0 needs no transfusion; that is usually considered below 8 g/dL.
So the correct pairing is this mother with anti-D immunoglobulin.
